questions.question: Who among the Mauryan ruler pioneered the propagation of Buddhism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka **was one of the most famous **Mauryan rulers** who ruled from** 268 to 232 BCE.**
 
• He is known for his conversion to Buddhism and his efforts to spread the religion throughout his empire.
 
• **After **a brutal **battle In Kalinga **in **261 BCE**, he became disillusioned with the violence and bloodshed that he had witnessed.
 
• He **turned to Buddhism** as a way to find inner peace and to promote nonviolence and compassion.
 
• He issued edicts that promoted religious tolerance, urged his subjects to follow the principles of Buddhism, and built monuments and shrines to honor the Buddha.
 
• He **sent missionaries** to neighboring kingdoms and even as far as **Greece** and **Egypt**.
 
• He also convened the famous** Third Buddhist Council** in** 250 BC** at **Pataliputra, Bihar,** which helped to codify the teachings of the Buddha and to promote a more unified Buddhist community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samparti **was 5th ruler of the Mauryan Empire and the** ****grandson of Ashoka.**

 
 
• He is regarded for his **patronage and efforts to spread Jainism** in East India.
 
 
 
• **Devavarman **7th Emperor of the Maurya Empire.
 
 
• He **patronized Hinduism**.
 
 
 
• **Bindusara **was the** father of Ashoka** and the son of the **dynasty's founder Chandragupta Maurya.**
 
 
• The Buddhist texts **Samantapasadika** and **Mahavamsa **suggest that **he followed Brahmanism**.

questions.question: Licensing policy of the government was primarily aimed to promote _______ .

options.text: development of schools and hospitals in smaller states
growth of textiles in southern part of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**regional equality.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The licensing policy** of the government was introduced **to regulate the industrial sector** and **ensure fair competition among businesses**. It aimed to control the establishment, expansion, and operation of industries through a licensing system.
 
• The **primary objective of the licensing policy was to promote regional equality** and** balanced economic development across different states** and regions of the country.
 
• It sought to prevent the concentration of industries in a few regions and encourage their dispersal in less-developed areas.
 
• Another objective of the licensing policy was to** promote import substitution and self-reliance in the economy.**
 
 
• It encouraged the production of goods and services within the country and discouraged their importation from abroad.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Licensing Policy in India:**

 
• **Industrial licensing in India** is a mandatory rule put forth by the government of India for enterprises belonging to certain industries. 
 
• The licensing policy was **introduced in the Industrial Policy Resolution(IPR) of 1956** to **promote regional equality.**
 
• The rule was passed under the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, of 1951**, also known as IDR Act.
 
• Under this policy, private entrepreneurs were required to obtain a government license before establishing a new industry or expanding an existing one.
 
• It also aimed to protect the interests of small-scale industries and prevent the domination of large corporations.
 
• It had **some drawbacks** too as
 
 
• Bureaucratic delays, corruption, and rent-seeking behavior among officials and businessmen were caused by it.
 
• It also stifled innovation and efficiency in the industrial sector by creating entry barriers and limiting competition.

questions.question:
What best defines prokaryotic cells?

I. Single chromosome

II. Membrane-bound cell organelles absent
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prokaryotic cells** are** unicellular organisms** that **lack a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles** in their cytoplasm.
 
• The genetic material of prokaryotic cells is present in a **single circular chromosome** that is** not enclosed within a membrane**.
 
• They are generally smaller in size than eukaryotic cells and have a simpler structure.
 
• They are found in **bacteria **and **archaea**, which are two of the three domains of life on Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eukaryotic **and **Prokaryotic** cells are the two main types of cells that make up living organisms.
 
• Here are the key differences between them:

 
 

 **Part**
 **Eukaryotic cells**
 **Prokaryotic cells**
 
 

 **Nucleus**
 have a true nucleus, their genetic material is enclosed within a membrane-bound nucleus.
 lack a true nucleus, genetic material is present in a region called the nucleoid, which is not enclosed by a membrane.
 
 

 Membrane-bound organelles
 have membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi apparatus.
 lack membrane-bound organelles.
 
 

 **Chromosomes**
 most have multiple linear chromosomes.
 have just one circular chromosome.
 
 

 Reproduction
 by **mitosis **(for somatic cells) or **meiosis **(for sex cells).
 by **binary fission**.
 
 

 DNA Structure
 Linear DNA is complexed with histone proteins, present in the nucleus.
 Circular DNA is found in the nucleoid region, without histone proteins.
 
 

 **Examples**
 plants, animals, fungi, and protists.
 bacteria and archaea.

__
 
• **Article 71** of the Constitution of India deals with **"Matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President". **

• (a) **elected members of both Houses** of Parliament and of
 
• (b) **elected members of the Legislative Assemblies** of the States.
 
 
 
• The President is elected for a **term of five years** and is eligible for re-election.
 
• According to **Article 66**, The **Vice-President of India is elected by** an Electoral College consisting of the **members(elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament**.
 
 
• The Vice-President is also elected for a term of five years and can be re-elected.

• **Article 70 **deals with the **Discharge of the President's functions in other contingencies**.
 
 
• Parliament may make such provision as it thinks fit for the discharge of the functions of the President in any contingency not provided for at another place.
 
 
 
• **Article 68** deals with the **Time of holding an election to fill vacancies in the office of Vice-President** and the term of office of the person elected to fill the casual vacancy.
 
 
• An election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of Vice-President shall be completed before the expiration of the term.
 
• An election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President occurring because of his death, resignation or removal, or otherwise shall be held as soon as possible after the occurrence of the vacancy, and the person elected to fill the vacancy shall, subject to the provisions of article 67, be entitled to hold office for the full term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.

questions.question: A boat can travel at a speed of 30 km/h in still water. If the flow of the stream is 2 km/h. How long will it take by the boat to travel 56 km upstream?

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream
